item.title: Multiple people dead as flooding continues in Indiana
item.description: Some parts of Indiana received more than 11 inches of rainfall over three days, beginning Aug. 11, causing record floods. Several suburbs of Indianapolis also underwater.

item.title: Lala is again a tropical storm, sending drenching rain and winds across Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm Sunday after skirting Hawaii without making landfall, but it wasn't done punishing the Big Island with hurricane-force gusts.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: As speed cameras spread to more states, so does the backlash from drivers
item.description: Millions of drivers across the country are encountering speed cameras for the first time, or will soon. Many don't like it, but advocates say there's clear evidence that cameras make roads safer.
item.content:encoded: Millions of drivers across the country are encountering speed cameras for the first time, or will soon. Many don't like it, but advocates say there's clear evidence that cameras make roads safer.

item.title: After a historic drought, here's one way Colorado is keeping its taps running
item.description: After a historically dry winter, some Colorado towns are running out of drinking water, requiring extraordinary measures to keep taps flowing.

item.title: NPR Senior Podcast Challenge: Official Rules
Billions of sea stars have died. A Northwest tribe is trying to save the species
item.description: Sunflower sea stars are critically endangered in the Pacific Ocean. University of Washington researchers are working with the Samish Indian Nation to bring this 24-armed creature back from the brink of extinction.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's trial highlights gaps in understanding, treating postpartum psychosis
item.description: The high-profile murder trial of Lindsay Clancy's has put the condition in the spotlight. Women who have had it call for more research and understanding of a difficult mental illness.

item.title: Lake Powell and Lake Mead water levels hit record lows
item.description: The water levels of Lakes Powell and Mead are at record lows. What does that mean for the millions of people who rely on the country's two biggest reservoirs and the Colorado River that feeds them?

item.title: Hurricane Lala strengthens as it heads to Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lala is headed toward Hawaii's Big Island. If it makes landfall there, it'd be the first hurricane to do so since 1871.
